newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Aug M2 supply rises 17.4 pct on year - BOK.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Aug M2 supply rises 17.4 pct on year - BOK.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose a year-on-year 17.4 percent in August, against a 14.7 percent rise a year earlier, provisional Bank of Korea (BOK) figures showed on Thursday.
Note - M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. The BOK has stopped providing M2 figures in won.
A central bank official said the M2 money supply would rise about 17.5 percent year-on-year in September, against a 13.9 percent rise a year ago.
"Corporate operating expenses are rising because of a slowdown in exports and domestic sales," said Park Chul, a senior BOK official.
He said the M2 rise in August was higher than a year ago because of the maturity extension for trust accounts at banks.
The amount of money in trust accounts had fallen by about 4.5 trillion won since May, when the maturity was extended to 1-1/2 years from one year, he said.
He said a rise in government spending and private-sector borrowings was a reason for the M2 rise in August.
In August, the state's budget spending was 1.43 trillion won more than budget revenue. A year ago, budget spending was 370 billion won higher than revenue.
Private sector credit grew by 3.54 trillion won in the month, compared with a rise of 2.56 trillion won a year ago.
Capital outflows were 1.9 trillion won larger than inflows from overseas in August. A year before inflows were 300 billion won more, the BOK statement said.
Net issues of certificates for deposits totalled 1.79 trillion won in August, against 634.7 billion won a year ago.
